plain_description.what: No calls. On the combined dataset (about 5,900 held-out questions, 18 models), the test measured how much knowing a question's tree cell improves prediction of which models answer correctly. It compared this with k-means cells and with 200 random cell sets of the same size within each source.
plain_description.why: It asks whether cells carry real information about model strengths beyond simply knowing which benchmark a question came from.
plain_description.information: Beating the random cells means the cells are meaningful. Beating k-means would favour the tree as an index. Result: done. The tree's cells carry clearly more information than random cells within the same source. But k-means did somewhat better than the tree as built, and about half of that gap comes from 191 questions the tree files under another source. All of this uses source labels ('source-conditioned'). It is predictive information, not a measured routing gain.
